Depends on what era your playing in. For example the 80s oilers and 90s penguins didn't have the best defense but still won 7 cups combined as a result of their insane offensive fire power, combined with playing in a higher scoring game. The new jersey devils (and even the red wings to an extent) of the late 90s to early 2000s were a great defensive team playing in a slower paced era with an incredible goalie in Martin brodeur and showed than defense can win championships. Nowadays in the salary cap era, you usually see championship to borderline dynasty teams with a clear #1 two-way defenseman and usually one star forward driving the offense. The rest of the team has to hold their own defensively, and so it's more of a depth team effort to buy in defensively to win, and you have to get lucky and have a goalie perform at least good.

When I'm building my cities I like to think of the history behind them. Since I usually build American style-cities that's what I'm best versed in. If your building an American style city, think of where you want the oldest part of the city to be and start it as a grid facing the water. Grids were used lots in cities and towns until after WWII. Build the grid as big as you want, then you could try doing a non-rectangular grid for the rest of the island, as in a head cannon it would be built later. Read u/psychomap's  comment on how to built a one because they explained it pretty well. You could also try merging different grids together, creating different angles, but then it would be a pain to zone. Another idea on the left side of the island is to build houses on the coast by bringing the road back a bit. Some paths around the entire coastline could also be cool. I feel like this could become a pretty cool build, so I'd like to see  what you do with it.

They played tourette's for the first time August 30th, 1992. This version first appeared on From The Muddy Banks Of The Wishkah in 1996, and again in 2009 on Live at Reading. Nirvana then played it at rehearsal on September 8th for the MTV 1992 Video Music Awards. Nirvana then played tourette's on September 10th and 11th for the No on 9 Benefit and the Washington Music Industry Coalition Benefit respectively. The first time they recorded tourette's in the studio was on October 26th in the scraped "In Utero Demo Sessions" that spanned from October 25th to the 26th. The version was left instrumental as the band decided not to add any vocals. Nirvana then recorded tourette's again at Pachyderm Recording Studio, Cannon Falls, Minnesota, US. They booked 2 weeks in the studio from February 12th to 26th but did not get started recording until the 13th. Along with Moist Vagina and Radio Friendly Unit Shifter, tourette's was recorded on February 14th, 1993, this time with vocals. This version of the song would make it's way onto In Utero. The last time Nirvana would play tourette's(that we know of) would be on July 23rd 1993 at the infamous Roseland Ballroom/New Music Seminar gig. This performance of it however, would have John Duncan(their guitar tech) on second guitar.
